findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink didn't have water available, nor was the hot water tank functional. There was a potable water source on site that provided clean water to the storage tank, however, the water heater remained unfunctional. SCDPH will follow-up on the mobile unit's next operating event for warm water for handwashing.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket was tested at 100ppm (quat). The employees mentioned that solution was provided by the dispenser at the brick and mortar. Discussed that the concentration was too low and needed to be at least 200ppm to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces. The inspector was able to get more Sani tablets from a different vendor to add to the concentration to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: There was no stem thermometer available for measuring internal foods temperatures. PIC assured inspectors that the thermometer will be present in the future. Ensure that there is always a stem thermometer is available for measuring the internal temperatures of mood items.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There was no test strips available during inspection. PIC acquired test strips during the inspection. Ensure that there is always test strips available to monitor the concentration of sanitizers.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Based on the number of violations (priority and priority foundation) and lack of knowledge demonstrated by employees, managers aren’t performing duties correctly as required. Several TCS food items were found to be in violation due to improper holding temperatures. See violations #21 and #22 for further details. None of the required paper work could be located at the time of the inspection. This includes manager and food handler certifications, employee reporting forms, and norovirus response procedures. Test strips were also not available to test sanitizer concentrations. Follow-ups for the violations have been scheduled for 11/12/2024 to ensure that corrective actions take place. Be sure that education is provided to employees on who to report to if they’re sick, proper temperature control for food items, certifications, and overall preventative measures to ensure food safety. 

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
None of the employees were food handler or manager certified. Individuals who are not Food Manager Certified must have a food handler’s certification if handling or preparing food. Ensure that employees obtain a food handler’s certification if they’re not manager certified. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
There were no signed employee health forms located on the mobile unit. PIC mentioned that signed forms were at the restaurant. Ensure that signed reporting agreements are available and can be easily located for future inspections. 
 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Written procedures for responding to vomit/diarrheal events could not be located at time of inspection. Bleach was also not available. Ensure that written procedures for responding to a vomit/diarrheal (and bleach) are available and can be conveniently located for future inspections  

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Several meats stored in a warmer were tempting between 54F-60F (probed). These foods include but aren't limited to cooked chicken, steak, and ground beef. The warmer appeared to not have electrical power. As a result, the meats were not going to be used for service. Ensure that TCS food items are 135F or above to maintain proper hot holding temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Several TCS food items inside a prep cooler were tempting between 57F-71F (probed). These items include but aren't limited to shredded cheese, mayonnaise, sour cream, shredded lettuce, and diced tomatoes. PIC mentioned that foods were placed in the cooler two hours prior to the inspection. Time control was placed on all TCS food items. Due to the mobile unit’s operating hours (5pm-9pm), all TCS foods were able to be used for service but any leftovers must be dumped at the end of the night. PIC mentioned that the cooler will be getting serviced soon. Ensure that all TCS foods stored in cold holding units are maintained at 41F or less. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
The only prep cooler stored on the mobile truck wasn't functioning properly. Several food items inside the cooler were tempting between 57F-71F (probed). These items include but aren't limited to shredded cheese, mayonnaise, sour cream, shredded lettuce, and diced tomatoes. PIC mentioned that foods were placed in the cooler two hours prior to the inspection. Time control was placed on all TCS food items. Due to the mobile unit’s operating hours (5pm-9pm), all TCS foods were able to be used for service but any leftovers must be dumped at the end of the night. PIC mentioned that the cooler will be getting serviced soon. Ensure that cold holding units are sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow-up on 11/12/2024. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
None of the employees were food handler or manager certified. Individuals who are not Food Manager Certified must have a food handler’s certification if handling or preparing food. Ensure that employees obtain a food handler’s certified if they’re not manager certified. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.
